title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Morgan Rivera
summary: Comprehensive people-ops playbook covering end-to-end hiring, new-employee onboarding (0-90 days), performance and feedback cycles, probation and promotion guidance, and manager responsibilities. Includes templates, checklists, timelines, and escalation points.
body:
Purpose

This playbook is a single-point reference for Redwood Inference managers and people-ops partners to run consistent, fair, and efficient hiring, onboarding, and performance processes. It codifies our expectations, timelines, templates, and ownership so every candidate and employee receives a predictable experience.

Scope

Applies to all full-time and long-term contract hires across engineering, product, go-to-market, and corporate functions. Temporary/short-term contractors and intern programs follow a simplified variant (see related pages).

Table of contents
1. Hiring process overview
2. Interview stages and scorecards
3. Offer, background, and onboarding kickoff
4. New hire 0-90 day onboarding plan (checklist)
5. Performance & feedback cycle (annual + ad-hoc)
6. Probation, promotion, and compensation guidance
7. Manager responsibilities & templates
8. Escalations and exceptions

1) Hiring process overview

High-level goals:
- Time-to-offer target: 28 days from requisition approval to offer acceptance for engineering roles (phone screen to offer).
- Candidate experience NPS target: >= 80.
- Interview-to-hire ratio target: <= 8:1.

Owner & stakeholders:
- Requisition owner: Hiring manager (HM) — accountable for role definition, shortlists, and hiring decision.
- People Ops recruiter: Sourcing, scheduling, coordination, offer administration.
- Interview panel: Cross-functional interviewers assigned per role.
- Hiring committee (for IC level >= L4 / manager hires): Final calibration and approval.

Step-by-step process (standard):
1. Requisition approval: HM submits req with role description, level, compensation band, and justification. People Ops approves and assigns recruiter.
2. Sourcing & screening: Recruiter sources, performs recruiter screen and schedules HM screen.
3. Interview loop: 3-5 interviews (technical, system design/role-specific, product judgment, collaboration/culture). Use the role-specific scorecard (section 2).
4. Debrief & decision: Panel completes scorecards within 24 hours. HM convenes debrief and makes hiring decision.
5. Offer: Recruiter prepares offer package (base, equity, start date, benefits). HM approves and offer extended.
6. Background & reference checks: Initiated by People Ops upon verbal acceptance.
7. Onboarding kickoff: New hire invited to onboarding calendar, buddy assigned, necessary access requested.

Diversity & fairness checklist (mandatory):
- Diverse interview panel for senior hires (>=2 different teams / 40% gender/ethnic diversity where possible).
- Structured interviews and scorecards required; avoid off-the-cuff gating questions.
- Reasonable accommodations offered and documented.

2) Interview stages and scorecards

Required interview types (engineering example):
- Recruiter screen (30m): role fit, salary expectations, simple verification.
- Hiring manager screen (45m): scope, experience, career goals.
- Technical screen (60m): coding/data structures or domain-relevant assessment.
- System design / architecture (60-75m) for senior roles.
- Collaboration & culture (45m): cross-team collaboration, communication, ownership.

Scorecard (mandatory fields for every interview):
- Role: technical/product/ops
- Strengths (3 bullets)
- Gaps / concerns
- Behavioral examples tied to rubric
- Recommend: Strong Yes / Yes / Borderline / No
- Leveling notes (if applicable)
- Confidence (1-5)

Example numeric rubric (used by hiring committee):
- Technical competence (1-5)
- Problem decomposition (1-5)
- Impact & execution (1-5)
- Collaboration & communication (1-5)
- Cultural alignment (1-5)

Calibration & leveling:
- Hiring committee convenes for any senior hires or disputed decisions. Committee uses anonymized scorecards and leveling examples to reduce bias.

3) Offer, background, and onboarding kickoff

Offer packet checklist:
- Offer letter PDF (HR template)
- Compensation breakdown (base, sign-on, equity, target bonus if applicable)
- Benefits summary and enrollment deadlines
- Employment agreement / contractor MSA as applicable

Background checks & legal compliance:
- People Ops initiates background checks after verbal acceptance; conditional offers contingent on clearance for regulated roles.
- Immigration/work-authorization: HR verifies visa status and coordinates sponsorship where applicable.

Onboarding kickoff (what recruiter sets up):
- Start date confirmation and 1st-week calendar invite with orientation sessions
- Slack channel and buddy assignment
- Access requests to core systems (G Suite, Redwood Console dev spaces, HRIS, laptop provisioning ticket)

4) New hire 0-90 day onboarding plan (owner: hiring manager + buddy + people-ops)

Principles:
- Clear goals, measurable outcomes and early wins
- Frequent synchronous feedback in first 30 days, structured check-ins at day 7, 30, 60, 90
- Pairing with a buddy to accelerate cultural and tooling ramp

Day 0-7 (orientation & fundamentals):
- Complete HR paperwork and benefits enrollment
- Equipment delivered & validated (laptop, dongles, primary access)
- IT & security training completed (MFA, SSO, data handling)
- Introductory meetings: manager 1:1, team standup, buddy intro, product overview
- Assign first small orientation task (documentation update, runbook read-through)

Day 8-30 (ramp & contribution):
- Technical onboarding: repo walkthroughs, local dev setup, CI/CD checklist
- Shadow customer issues or incidents (if applicable) to learn product and SLOs
- Deliverable: shipping a small change / PR (owner: HM).
- Manager check-in (30m) at day 30: discuss progress, blockers, and career goals.

Day 31-60 (autonomy & deeper context):
- Ownership of a well-scoped ticket or sub-project with measurable success criteria
- Start of 1:1 weekly coaching cadence with manager
- Training plan for role-specific skills (quantization profiles, infra concepts, etc.)
- Midpoint feedback session at day 60 (written notes shared by manager).

Day 61-90 (impact & evaluation):
- Deliver the agreed project or measurable impact (latency improvement, doc deliverable, etc.)
- 90-day review meeting: HM presents evaluation with buddy and people-ops present (if requested).
- Outcome: confirmed hire, extended probation steps (if needed), or separated with offboarding checklist.

Onboarding checklists (to be maintained as living checklist in HRIS):
- Accesses granted (list of services)
- Required trainings completed (security, compliance, code of conduct)
- Local dev environment status
- First shipped PR or business deliverable
- 30/60/90 feedback artifacts stored in HRIS

5) Performance & feedback cycle

Annual cycle overview:
- Quarter-by-quarter continuous feedback encouraged; formal cycles occur twice per year with an annual performance calibration for compensation cycle.
- Typical cadence: mid-year check-in (informal but documented), end-of-year performance review and calibration (formal).

Roles and responsibilities:
- Manager: collects examples, runs 1:1s, documents feedback, completes performance form, recommends calibration and compensation changes.
- Employee: prepares a self-assessment summarizing achievements, blockers and career goals.
- People Ops: runs calibration meetings, enforces fairness checks, and communicates final outcomes.

Review mechanics:
1. Self-assessment (employee)
2. Manager assessment + documented examples
3. Peer feedback (optional but encouraged)
4. Calibration meeting (manager + peer managers + people-ops)
5. Compensation council (if compensation action recommended)

Feedback best practices:
- Use SBI (Situation-Behavior-Impact) format for actionable feedback.
- Combine frequent short feedback with formal documented assessments.
- Avoid surprises — managers must surface concerns early (ideally within first 30 days of observed issue).

Performance ratings and consequences:
- Rating bands: Exceeds Expectations / Meets Expectations / Needs Improvement / Unsatisfactory.
- Needs Improvement triggers a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) only after documented coaching attempts and clear objectives. PIP owner: manager with People Ops oversight.

6) Probation, promotion, and compensation guidance

Probation (new hires):
- Standard probation window: 90 days for most hires; extended to 6 months for some senior or regulated roles.
- Probation outcomes: Confirmed, Extended Probation (with specific objectives), or Termination (with HR review).

Promotion & leveling guidance:
- Promotion recommended when an employee consistently demonstrates the next level's competencies across scope, impact, and leadership (for ICs) or team outcomes (for managers).
- Promotion packet (manager responsibility) must include: rationale, impact examples, updated role description, proposed comp band, and peer references.
- Promotions considered at quarterly calibration cycles. Emergency promotions possible for exceptional contributions with executive approval.

Compensation adjustments:
- Managed by People Ops and compensation committee during scheduled cycles.
- Manager can propose off-cycle adjustments for retention risks; must include market data and documented justification.

7) Manager responsibilities & templates

Core manager responsibilities (summary):
- Hire the right people: define role, build panels, run debriefs, and make final call.
- Onboard effectively: own 0-90 plan, create measurable first deliverables, and perform scheduled check-ins.
- Feedback & development: run weekly 1:1s, document coaching moments, complete formal reviews.
- Reliability & escalation: maintain on-call rotations for teams, update runbooks, and escalate incidents per oncall runbook.

Templates and example language (quick copy):
- Interview feedback snippet: "Candidate demonstrated strong system decomposition and trade-off reasoning. Concerns: limited distributed systems experience at scale. Recommend: hire at L3 with targeted onboarding plan to ramp infra knowledge."
- 30/60/90 check-in note header: "Progress, Blockers, Next 30 Days, Manager Actions"
- PIP objective example: "Increase PR throughput by 25% over 60 days by addressing identified CI bottlenecks and mentoring two team members; success measured by PR closure metrics and peer feedback."

Manager escalation flow:
- HR-question: people-ops@example.internal -> People Ops partner triages.
- Performance concern: manager -> people-ops -> Head of People Ops for PIP approvals.
- Compensation exception: manager -> People Ops -> Compensation Committee.

8) Escalations and exceptions

Common exceptions and how to handle:
- International hiring longer timelines (visa sponsorship): start recruiting earlier (+6-12 weeks) and route offers through Legal.
- High-volume hiring spurs: use recruiting surge playbook and hire contract sourcers; maintain standard scorecards.
- Role re-leveling mid-recruit: HM must pause loop and notify people-ops; update scorecards and re-run interviews if applicable.

Audit & compliance notes:
- Maintain offer and interview artifacts for at least 2 years per company retention policy.
- Store final performance review documents and promotion packets in HRIS with access restricted to manager, HR partner, and People Ops leadership.

Appendices
A. Quick interview scheduling template (email)
B. New-hire orientation sample 1-week calendar
C. Interview scorecard PDF template (link in related pages)
D. List of role-specific ramp resources (engineering: repo index, infra runbook, benchmarking guide)

Document ownership & updates
- Primary owner: People Ops (Morgan Rivera). Content must be reviewed annually or when policy changes.
- Last updated: 2026-01-18.
